evidence.text: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) represent the most clinically advanced non-viral system for the delivery of RNAs, including messenger RNA (mRNA) and small interfering RNA (siRNA).
To date, the U.S.
Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved four LNP-based therapeutics: Comirnaty, Spikevax, mRESVIA, and Onpattro.
Among these clinical products, Onpattro is the only therapeutic that utilizes systemic administration as the route of delivery [1].

Although LNPs can be a promising tool for the delivery of nucleic acids for protein replacement therapy [2], gene editing [3], and in situ cell therapy [4], these therapeutic applications are limited by LNPs’ predominant liver accumulation, particularly in liver hepatocytes, upon systemic delivery [5,6].

evidence.text: In summary, this study extends the current framework of LNP-mediated nucleic acid delivery by demonstrating that the structure of lipid tails can drive extrahepatic delivery through modulating LNP surface hydrophobicity.

While our findings were primarily derived from dendrimer-based systems, we observed consistent hydrophobicity-driven trends in LNPs formulated with clinically approved ionizable lipids SM-102 and ALC-0315 (Fig.
2J–L), supporting the broader applicability of this mechanism across LNP platforms.
Further investigations across additional lipid platforms will be valuable to fully establish the generalizability of this principle.

Notably, although 50% series dLNPs exhibited superior transfection efficiency compared to their 100% series counterparts in vitro in the absence of serum proteins, their overall in vivo transfection potency was markedly lower (Supplementary 3, Figs.
S1 and S2).

Additionally, while in vitro cytotoxicity screening was performed to select lead formulations with high relative cell viability prior to in vivo studies, and no acute toxicity was observed in animals at the administered dose, a comprehensive biosafety evaluation including assessment of liver and kidney function and systemic inflammatory responses was not conducted.

As the primary focus of this work was to elucidate the mechanistic role of surface hydrophobicity in modulating the nano-bio interface and tissue-selective delivery, detailed toxicological characterization of the dLNP platform remains an important direction for future investigation.
